nodes.label: Patient in their 70s presented with dyspnea and fatigue
Medical history: no structural heart disease or hypertension; diffuse large B-cell lymphoma diagnosed 4 years ago, treated with 8 courses of chemotherapy
Physical examination: blood pressure 96/54 mm Hg, heart rate 56 bpm
Echocardiography reveals diffuse right atrial masses
PET-CT shows increased metabolic activity along the right atrial myocardium/pericardium
Relapsed diffuse large B-cell lymphoma with cardiac involvement
Lymphoma relapse causing right heart dysfunction
Histopathological biopsy/immunohistochemistry and pericardial fluid cytology/flow cytometry have not yet been obtained
Pathologist identifies histopathological biopsy/immunohistochemistry and pericardial fluid cytology/flow cytometry as the gold standard for confirming cardiac lymphoma relapse
Radiologist analysis concludes imaging and lab findings strongly support cardiac lymphoma relapse involving the right atrium/pericardium rather than chemotherapy cardiotoxicity

Pathologist analysis independently concludes cardiac lymphoma relapse (right atrium/pericardium) is the most credible hypothesis, while chemotherapy cardiotoxicity, endocrine/metabolic disorder, and sepsis/opportunistic infection lack support
Laboratory physician analysis independently supports relapsed DLBCL with cardiac involvement and confirms imaging/lab evidence are fully covered
Pathologist recommends expedited biopsy and clinical correlation due to retrieval limits
